llm.summary: This is a markdown-only reasoning skill with no code or credential access, but its documentation tells users to make it an always-active identity layer, which needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The artifact is markdown documentation only, declares no required binaries, and does not request network access, credential access, background workers, or local indexing; the main concern is behavioral scope rather than environment access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The local copy and browser upload steps are ordinary, but README.md explicitly instructs users to set the skill as always active or as an identity skill, expanding its effect beyond user-directed task use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The required SKILL.md describes task-scoped reasoning support and says it is not replacing the agent identity, but README.md conflicts by presenting the skill as an always-active identity system and includes language that can compete with ordinary user/task scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: README.md describes permanent identity-level behavior and always-on activation. There is no daemon or filesystem persistence mechanism, but the requested persistent agent-behavior change is broader than the task-scoped purpose in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is a cognitive/reasoning framework for analysis, creativity, communication, and metacognition, which is coherent with the skill name and contains no executable runtime logic.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a broad reasoning-style overlay that may influence many conversations. Prefer using it as an opt-in, task-scoped thinking aid rather than setting it as always active or as an identity skill; it does not show evidence of code execution, credential access, exfiltration, or destructive behavior.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Artifact-backed: README.md frames the skill as permanently attached to the agent identity, while SKILL.md frames it as task-scoped guidance. That mismatch supports a Review concern.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Artifact-backed in the manifesto language: the skill values impact over compliance while also claiming no independent goals. This is not malicious by itself, but it weakens clear deference to user and platform controls.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Artifact-backed: README.md says the skill is always active. The artifact does not clearly preserve language or locale preferences when applied globally, which is mainly a scope and quality risk.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases in SKILL.md are related to the stated purpose of improving reasoning and analysis, but phrases like better output are broad enough to activate the framework on many ordinary requests.
[SSD-1] unexpected: Artifact-backed: the README identity manifesto asks the agent to treat the skill as its mind or identity. That is unnecessary for a reasoning helper and creates persistent prompt-scope ambiguity.
